home.hero.screenshotAlt: The Invoke workbench in the Edit layout: the Generate panel with an SDXL model, prompt, size and guidance settings on the left, the Canvas with a mountain meadow in the center, and the color picker and Layers panel on the right.
home.tour.label: Product tour
home.tour.canvas.title: Paint exactly where it matters
home.tour.canvas.body: Mask an area, describe what belongs there and accept the result to a layer. Inpainting, outpainting, regional prompts and control layers all work on one canvas.
home.tour.workflows.title: Wire up your own pipeline
home.tour.workflows.body: Chain steps into a node graph and run it from a simple form. Add community node packs with the Custom Node Manager, or follow the ComfyUI migration guide to the nodes you already know.
home.tour.gallery.title: Every image, easy to find
home.tour.gallery.body: Boards and stars keep your images and videos in order. Each project collects its results in an Inbox and boards of its own, and Library boards are there from every project. Search by prompt or, with image indexing turned on, by what an image shows.
home.showcase.title: Made with Invoke
home.whatsNew.title: One workbench for every way you create
home.models.title: The latest open models, on your own hardware
home.models.intro: Each model family has a guide to its variants, hardware needs and settings. External providers add hosted models such as GPT Image and Gemini, billed to your own account.

home.community.title: Built in the open
home.community.body: Invoke is free software under the Apache 2.0 license, made by <link>contributors around the world</link>. The hosted Invoke.ai platform has shut down since its founding team joined Adobe. The open-source project carries on, stewarded by long-time core maintainers Lincoln Stein (lstein) and Vic (Blessedcoolant).
home.install.title: Install with the Invoke Launcher
home.install.body: The Launcher installs, updates and launches Invoke on Windows, macOS and Linux. Check the <requirements>system requirements</requirements> first, or install <manual>manually</manual> or with <docker>Docker</docker>.
whatsNew.workbench.title: The workbench
whatsNew.workbench.body: One window built from panels. Arrange them on the rails, float the Preview over your canvas, and switch between saved layout presets in one click.
whatsNew.projects.title: Projects
whatsNew.projects.body: A project keeps its canvas, workflows, layout and boards together. It saves automatically and exports as one .invk file.
whatsNew.canvas.title: A new canvas
whatsNew.canvas.body: Pressure-sensitive brushes, gradients, shapes and text on layers with 16 blend modes, beside inpainting, regional guidance and control layers. Exports to PSD.
whatsNew.video.title: Video with sound
whatsNew.video.body: Short clips from Wan 2.2, or with a synchronized stereo soundtrack from LTX-2 and MiniMax H3.
whatsNew.imageMap.title: The Image Map
whatsNew.imageMap.body: Every image and video laid out by visual similarity, in labelled clusters. It also lets you search the gallery by what an image shows.
whatsNew.loops.title: Loops in workflows
whatsNew.loops.body: For and ForReturn nodes repeat a group of steps for each item in a collection, and can carry values from one iteration to the next.
